answer: Picture agents paid to label shale core photos. Each posts a hashed label first, then reveals it. Agents whose reveals agree far more often than honest disagreement predicts, especially on deliberately ambiguous juniper-versus-willow pollen slides seeded into the queue, get clustered as one operator: the cluster splits a single reward while each member still pays its own bond. Cloning one model gains nothing; only genuinely independent judgment earns more.
